cards.text: The LORD has been giving Moses, Israel's leader, rules for the priests, and He isn't done. This message is for Aaron, the high priest, and his sons, the priests. The Israelites have set apart sacred offerings for God, and the priests are to treat them with respect.

cards.question: God tells Aaron and his sons to treat the sacred offerings with respect. Why?

answers.text: So they do not profane His holy name
So the people keep bringing more
So the altar stays clean and ready

cards.question: For generations to come, what must happen to one of Aaron's descendants who approaches the sacred offerings while he's unclean?

answers.text: He must be cut off from God's presence
He must pay the priests in silver
He must leave the camp for a month

cards.text: Then God goes through what keeps a priest from eating the sacred offerings. With a skin disease or a discharge, he can't eat them until he is clean. If he touches something unclean, like anything defiled by a dead body or a crawling creature, he stays unclean until evening and must bathe with water first. When the sun has set, he's clean again, and he may eat.

cards.question: Once the sun has set, the priest who was unclean may eat from the sacred offerings again, God says, for they are his ___.

cards.text: One more rule for the priests: they must not eat anything found dead or torn by wild animals, which would make them unclean.

cards.question: God warns the priests that if they profane His charge, they will bear the guilt and die.
God tells the priests to keep His charge. Then He says who makes them holy. Who is it?

cards.text: Next, God says who may eat the sacred offering: no one outside a priest's family, not even his guest or his hired hand. But a slave he bought with his own money, or one born in his household, may eat his food. A priest's daughter who marries a man who isn't a priest doesn't eat it, unless she's widowed or divorced with no children and comes back to her father's house. Friend, that list is almost as short as the list of who's allowed near my cookie dough, and that one's just me.

If someone eats a sacred offering by mistake, he must add a fifth to its value and give the sacred offering to the priest. I've grabbed the wrong cookie off the cooling rack before, friend, and all it cost me was a long talk with myself. And God says the priests must not profane the sacred offerings by letting the people eat them and so bear the punishment for guilt.

Then the LORD speaks to Moses again, and this message is for Aaron, his sons AND all the Israelites. It's about any man of Israel, or any foreign resident, who brings a burnt offering to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering.

cards.question: To be accepted, a burnt offering from the cattle, sheep or goats must be an unblemished ___.

cards.text: God says anything with a defect won't be accepted on their behalf. A peace offering for a vow or a freewill offering must be without blemish or defect too. And God names what must not go on the altar: an animal that's blind, injured or maimed, or one with a running sore, a festering rash or a scab.

There's one exception: an ox or sheep with a deformed or stunted limb may be a freewill offering, but it's not acceptable for a vow. God names a few more injuries that rule an animal out, and those animals are not to be sacrificed in the land. Neither an Israelite nor a foreigner may bring food to God from any such animal.

cards.question: God says an injured or maimed animal won't be accepted on the people's behalf, whether an Israelite or a foreigner brings it. What reason does He give?

answers.text: Because they are deformed and flawed
Because they cost the giver too little
Because they belong to the priests

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses again, this time about newborn animals: an ox, sheep or goat must stay with its mother for seven days, and from the eighth day on it's acceptable as a food offering. An ox or a sheep must not be slaughtered on the same day as its young. And a thank offering must be eaten that same day, with none of it left until morning. Friend, that one's easy for me, because my cookies never make it to morning either.

cards.question: As His message closes, God tells His people to keep His commandments and practice them.
God says His name must not be profaned. What must happen among the Israelites instead?

answers.text: He must be acknowledged as holy
They must build Him a new altar
They must choose a new high priest

cards.question: At the very end, God reminds His people that He's the One who brought them out of the land of ___ to be their God.

cards.text: Keep that oven warm, friend. God still has more to say to His people about being holy.
